name.en-US: The Major Legend of St. Francis

description.la: Vita S. Francisci a S. Bonaventura, ministro generali, ex mandato Capituli Narbonensis (1260) conscripta, anno 1266 ab Ordine unica legenda recepta.
description.en-US: The official life of St. Francis, written by the Minister General St. Bonaventure for the Chapter of Narbonne (1260) and adopted in 1266 as the only legend of the Order: fifteen chapters on his life, with ten chapters of miracles after his death. The Latin is the text of the Fonti francescane, with its scriptural cross-references. The English of the prologue and the fifteen chapters is E. Gurney Salter's (1904). description.pt-BR: A biografia oficial de São Francisco, escrita por São Boaventura, ministro geral, e adotada pela Ordem em 1266 como única legenda: quinze capítulos sobre a vida e dez sobre os milagres póstumos.

la.editor: Quaracchi (PP. Collegii S. Bonaventurae), after the Fonti francescane transcription

sources.edition: Text of the Quaracchi edition (Legendae duae de vita S. Francisci, 1898) as transcribed by M. Mastrorilli for the Biblioteca digitale Fonti francescane (rilievo.poliba.it, 2003), read from the Wayback Machine snapshot of 2005-11-11.
sources.description: Lines of numbered sentence units are joined into the sections of the edition; the modern "cfr." scriptural cross-references of the transcription stay in parentheses; stray grave and acute accents of the web transcription are removed.
sources.tierEvidence: Bonaventure died in 1274; the Latin is his text. The web transcription is an anonymous digitization for scholarly use.

sources.edition: The Life of St. Francis by St. Bonaventure, translated by E. Gurney Salter (1904), as reset in The Little Flowers, The Mirror of Perfection, and St. Bonaventure's Life of St. Francis (London: J. M. Dent, Everyman's Library, 1910).
sources.description: Archive.org OCR read from the word-coordinate file and cleaned by script, not proofread; running heads and page numbers dropped, Salter's paragraph numbers kept. The Everyman volume prints the prologue and the fifteen chapters only: the Miracula after death are Latin only.
